summary: Built on the operator-led positioning agreed in week 1 to write the value proposition for founders and a separate message for corporate finance advisers. We agreed a named 100-day plan as the core promise and a two-track messaging structure. Case studies are blocked on management consent.

discussion.keyPoints: Helen said founders care most about who will sit on their board, not the fund. Mark noted founders often confuse Calder with the debt funds and assume heavy leverage.
Advisers want certainty of completion. Mark pointed out that 3 of the last 4 Calder deals closed on the terms in the indicative offer, which nobody outside the firm knows.
Both were keen to use portfolio growth numbers but Helen was cautious about naming companies without the management teams agreeing.

recommendations.recommendation: Lead with: capital plus a named operating partner and a written 100-day plan for every new investment.
Run two message tracks, one for founders and one for corporate finance advisers. The adviser track leads with 3 of the last 4 deals closing on agreed terms.
Publish four anonymised portfolio case studies, starting with the industrial services business that grew revenue 2.4x under Calder ownership.
Frame founder conversations around the cost of delaying succession planning, including the lower multiple a business gets without a step-up management team.

actions.action: Ask the four portfolio CEOs for consent to use their results in case studies

nextFocus: Plan how Calder generates more proprietary deal flow alongside adviser-led processes.
nextPreparation: Bring a list of the corporate finance advisers sending deals in the last two years and how many each sent.

tests.question: What did we agree is the core promise to founders?
What is the lead message for corporate finance advisers?
Did we agree to use the cost of delaying succession in founder conversations?
